result.summary: Switches the format string parameter types in BaseIndex::FatalErrorf and LogConnectFailure to util::log::FormatString. This enables compile-time verification that logging format strings do not include trailing newlines.
result.problem: Functions that forward formatted messages to the logger without using util::log::FormatString risk including redundant trailing newlines, which can lead to escaped `\x0a` characters inside log messages.
evidence: PR description: "Both functions format a message that is ultimately logged, so it must not contain a redundant trailing newline. Otherwise, it could lead to escaped \x0a inside log messages."
result.scope_notes: Small refactoring across three files touching BaseIndex and connection failure logging.
result.card: Switches BaseIndex::FatalErrorf and LogConnectFailure to use util::log::FormatString for their format string arguments. This enforces compile-time checks that format strings omit trailing newlines, preventing escaped `\x0a` sequences from appearing in log output. The author notes this continues work from PR 36397.
uncertainties: Diff was not included in metadata, though the commit message and description specify the changes.

risk.why: A typo in a compile-time format string constraint would fail to compile rather than produce runtime node errors.
